text:
Gray and damp this midday, 48 degrees with a light northwest breeze, and it feels a couple degrees cooler than that. We're still stuck on the edge of that upper low to our north, so the showers have been on and off. The forecasters give us a 40 percent chance of a few more this afternoon, and the European model is wetter than that, so I'd keep the umbrella handy. Any of them would be light, under a tenth of an inch, though a stronger one could throw in some graupel and a quick burst of heavier rain. We top out near 51.

The sun sets at 4:31, so it gets dark early under those clouds. Tonight stays cloudy and cool, with a low around 40.

Tuesday looks much the same, near 51 again, with showers likely from about noon on and the best odds from 1 to 5 in the afternoon. Wednesday looks like the driest day of the stretch.

My call: grab the jacket and umbrella today, and get your Tuesday errands done before noon.

AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: More of the same dreary weather expected for the first half of the week. We remain on the periphery of upper low pressure centered near the Gaspe Peninsula early this morning, with patchy light rain and drizzle occurring across much of the region. This activity is associated with a shortwave trough rounding the base of the trough, and we'll see a series of these over the next 48-72 hours. As such, periods of showers will continue to plague the region, particularly today and then again Tuesday into Tuesday night. As has been the case, most of the precipitation will fall as rain, with areas AOA 2500 ft mixing with and/or changing to snow overnight and into the early morning hours. A reinforcing shot of cold air Tuesday night will bring snow levels as low as 1500 ft or so, mainly along the international border and the northern Adirondacks/Greens, and this is the best chance for seeing any accumulating snow below 2000 ft, though even then, it'll be pretty minimal. The cold pool aloft and some meager instability could allow for more robust showers to produce some graupel both this afternoon and Tuesday afternoon, along with brief moderately heavy rainfall. Daytime temperatures will be similar both days, mainly in the mid 40s to low 50s, with the southern St Lawrence/Champlain Valleys approaching the mid 50s Tuesday afternoon under increasing W/SW flow. These winds will be on the breezy side Tuesday and Tuesday evening, particularly at summit level and on the eastern slopes of the Adirondacks and central/southern Greens. Gusts to 30 mph will be possible in these locations, with 35 to 45+ mph atop the mountain summits. Wednesday is looking to be the driest day, with shower coverage to be confined to the Northeast Kingdom and mainly during the morning hours. Some sunshine might break through in the afternoon, but it will remain seasonably cool with highs remaining in the 40s to around 50F. KEY MESSAGE 2: A fairly messy weather pattern will prevail for the latter half of the week. Temperatures appear likely to be about the same from day-to-day with upper 30s to mid 40s during the day and 20s to lower 30s at night. A high amplitude ridge will build across the western US while a pair of shortwaves dig well into the southeastern US on Thursday. These will eventually interact with the persistent upper low to our north during the weekend. Depending on the exact track of surface low pressure, the interaction between the various upper vorts, and which will be most intense will affect the outlook for Friday into Saturday. Given the broad, disorganized nature of the upper level features, it seems likely that the thermal gradient and active subtropical jet could be the deciding factors, which would favor suppressed, southern solutions. However, raw ensemble probabilities (both statistical, AI-driven and physics- based forecasts) suggest it is worth monitoring the potential for accumulating snow in our forecast area. WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Monday! Today features a continuation of gray and cloudy skies with periods of on-and-off showers. I think the bulk of the rain shower activity comes through the first half of the day, but there could still be a few spotty showers into the second half of the day. High temperatures for the day are climbing back into the 40s to about 50 this afternoon. Tuesday could feature some sunny breaks early on, but clouds and showers start to make their return into Tuesday afternoon and evening. Between today and Tuesday, most places don’t receive all that much rain—only a couple tenths of an inch. Temperatures are again in the 40s to nearly 50 for Tuesday afternoon. Clouds remain stubborn all the way through midweek with mostly cloudy skies overhead for both Wednesday and Thursday. Temperatures start to turn a bit cooler, as they fall into the mid and upper 40s for Wednesday and the low to mid 40s by Thursday.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-08T23:24:00Z — same caveat): Cloudy, cool with scattered showers Monday — Monday will be mostly cloudy and cool as scattered showers continue. Additional mountain flakes are possible, especially for the summits. Highs reach the upper 40s, with a stiff northwest breeze. After a mostly dry start to Tuesday, another round of scattered showers comes through by afternoon. Highs reach the low 50s. Wednesday (Veterans Day) turns drier, with only a spot shower leftover. However, it will be cloudy and cool, with highs in the upper 40s. The late-week stretch looks quite chilly, as the jet stream dips farther south. Highs will be closer to 40, with lots of clouds. A storm system may bring a round of rain and elevation snow Friday into Saturday, but uncertainty remains with the track. Stay tuned for updates.
